content:
jordan: quick flag 1: after rolling client libs yesterday we're seeing a small but consistent chunk of requests with quota attribution labeled `unknown`. Console confirms requests hit expected model ids but tenant/bucket resolution failed for ~3% traffic. digging.

maria: Could this be the header rename that landed in the proxy last sprint? `X-Route-Hint` -> `X-Rd-Route`?

jordan: Exactly that. Our router accepts both at routing time, but the quota-mapper path only reads `X-Route-Hint` in one of the legacy code paths. Mixed fleet (new SDKs -> new header, old proxies -> old header) leads to miss.

sam: That would also explain region skew: edge-west still on old proxy and edge-eu on new. Two different headers present across hops. Can we do a quick server-side fallback so mapping tries the new header first?

jordan: I sketched a tiny hotfix: lookup order [`X-Rd-Route`, `X-Route-Hint`, `Route-Meta`] and canonicalize to single key. Must be careful not to double-assign when multiple headers are present.

maria: Agreed. Dedupe rule: take the first non-empty header according to whitelist order. Also add a count metric `quota.attribution.header_mismatch` with labels (env, edge) to measure how often both headers are present.

lee: From client libs POV we could ship a compatibility patch that writes both headers for a week. For example python shim: `headers['X-Rd-Route'] = headers.get('X-Rd-Route') or headers.get('X-Route-Hint')` and log single-use telemetry. But that's more churn than a server fallback. Thoughts?

jordan: Server fallback is lower-friction but we should ask SDKs to emit the compat header for one rolling week to accelerate recovery and make the backfill easier. Also add a first-use log event so we can measure how many SDKs still send old header.

ashley: Console implications: when we show `unknown` attribution rows we currently surface tooltip "routing header missing or unrecognized". If the server fallback resolves those rows after a backfill, historical rows may change. We need communications for billing and dashboards.

maria: Options for remediation: retro-run attribution on raw request logs for the impacted window (parquet), or mark rows as "recomputed" and show a diff. Retro-run last 48h seems reasonable and accurate.

sam: Let's gate retro-run on the new metric so we know the affected tenant set. Also implement a dry-run mode: compute attribution and write to a test column first so we can spot-check before swapping.

ci-bot: deploy-started: quota-service/header-fallback-v1 -> canary us-west-1 (job #8429)

lee: minor but important: TS client compact-encoding test used lowercase header names in some mocks and some proxies canonicalize to lowercase. Quota-service should normalize header names before lookup. Are we already doing that?

jordan: We lowercase header keys in the mapper, but add an integration matrix test (gcp-edge, aws-alb, nginx) with varying cases and multiple-hops to ensure normalization and no double-counting.

maria: Action items: (1) jordan land fallback + metric + canary (2) lee cut py/ts compat patch that emits fallback header and logs first-use event (3) sam create backfill dry-run and schedule retro-run for last 48h once metric confirms scope (4) ashley draft console help text and billing note and coordinate PMs.

jordan: I'll monitor the canary and post canary metrics here. If `quota.attribution.header_mismatch` > 1% relative to baseline we pause and revert.

ashley: pinging @pm-billing to triage possible billing adjustments; small tenant set may see attribution corrections for last 48h.

pm-billing: thanks, will prepare a short note and contact affected customers if retro-run changes invoices.

lee: One more follow-up: add a README snippet for SDK maintainers about header compatibility windows and remove shim after 7 days.

jordan: Good call. I'll include rollback windows in the PR. Will report status in 30m after canary metrics stabilize. Thanks team :thumbsup:
